bull_bear.body:
- scale: World's largest camphor manufacturer — evidence: installed capacity of 10,000 MT per annum achieved in 2022, increased to 12,000 MT per annum in March 2026
- cost position: Natural, renewable pine-based feedstock reduces exposure to petrochemical input cost swings compared with synthetic competitors — evidence: demand and market performance of the Company's pine chemical products are largely independent of crude oil prices and are therefore less exposed to fluctuations in the global petroleum market
- distribution: Dedicated FMCG go-to-market built by wholly owned subsidiary Mangalam Brands Private Limited across Modern Trade, e-commerce, General Trade, contract manufacturing/private label and CSD channels — evidence: MBPL recorded a turnover of Rs. 238.64 crore in FY 2025-26 across these channels
- brand: Registered consumer brands (Mangalam, CamPure) built through TV commercial campaigns in the religious/home-fragrance camphor category — evidence: MBPL turnover of Rs. 238.64 crore in FY 2025-26 attributed to organised retail, digital commerce and institutional business built on these brands
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material cost and supply risk — Profitability may be affected by fluctuations in the prices and availability of key raw materials, intermediates and chemicals used in the manufacturing process; disruption in supply or increased procurement costs could adversely impact operations and margins.
- Regulatory and compliance risk — The Company operates in a highly regulated industry subject to environmental, health, safety and chemical handling regulations; changes in applicable laws or compliance requirements may increase operational costs and necessitate additional investment.
- Market and competitive risk — The chemical industry is highly competitive with domestic and international players; intense competition, pricing pressure and changing customer preferences may affect market position and profitability.
- Demand risk — Demand for camphor and related products is influenced by consumer consumption patterns, festive demand, industrial applications and overall economic conditions; adverse demand changes may impact sales volumes and revenue.
- Foreign exchange risk — Exposure to currency exchange rate fluctuations from imports, exports and other international transactions could affect profitability and cash flows.
- Supply chain and logistics risk — Disruptions in transportation networks, port operations, shipping availability or global supply chains may impact timely procurement of raw materials and delivery of finished products.
- Operational and manufacturing risk — Manufacturing operations involve risks related to equipment breakdown, process disruptions, fire incidents, industrial accidents and unplanned shutdowns, which may affect production and financial performance.
- Environmental, health and safety risk — Chemical manufacturing involves handling hazardous substances and requires strict adherence to safety standards; failure to maintain effective safety systems may result in accidents, regulatory actions and reputational impact.

business.body: Mangalam Organics manufactures pine-based specialty chemicals including terpenes (Camphor, Isobornyl Acetate, Isoborneol, Dipentene, Sodium Acetate) and Synthetic Resins (Terpene Phenolic Resin, Alkyl Phenolic Resin, Rosin Esters), operating under a single reportable Chemicals segment sold to adhesives, paints and coatings, printing inks, paper, rubber, pharmaceuticals, fragrance and personal-care industries. outlook.body:
- Focus on manufacturing and marketing high-quality intermediate terpene products (Camphene, Isobornyl Acetate, Isoborneol) to international customers for paint, resin and fragrance applications.
- Once intermediate product quality is standardized, expand into downstream Pinene and Camphene derivatives (e.g. Myrcene, Dihydro Myrcenol) that offer richer, more specialised opportunities with healthier margins.
- Increase the range of Terpene Phenolic Resin products to cater to wider domestic customer needs and pursue product approvals with the global tyre and adhesive export market.
- For Alkyl Phenolic Resin, understand customer pain points, provide tailor-made products and introduce a wider range of quality products to enable registration with key distributors.
- For Rosin Modified Resin, explore import-substitution opportunities in adhesives and printing ink, and improve product quality to global standards to unlock export opportunities.
- Strengthen the domestic retail camphor segment through wholly owned subsidiary Mangalam Brands Private Limited, expanding camphor-led products across spirituality, home fragrance, personal spaces and everyday care.
- Continue focus on optimising production processes, improving capacity utilisation and strengthening operational controls across manufacturing facilities.
- Pursue sustainable growth through energy-efficient technologies, responsible resource management and greener manufacturing practices.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company became the world's largest camphor manufacturer in 2022 with an installed capacity of 10,000 MT per annum, and increased that capacity further in March 2026 to 12,000 MT per annum. Future expansion at the Kumbhivali (Raigad) manufacturing facility is being planned with a focus on transformation, energy optimization and capacity scaling to support growing domestic and international demand, though no specific new project, site or timeline beyond the camphor capacity increase is named.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Chemical industry demand is closely linked to global manufacturing activity, with trends in automotive, construction, electronics, consumer goods and infrastructure influencing overall demand.
- Structural shift towards specialty chemicals, sustainable products and high-value-added applications is accelerating adoption of green chemistry and energy-efficient manufacturing, which the Company expects to benefit from given its natural pine-based feedstock.
- India's chemical industry is expected to remain among the fastest-growing globally, supported by robust domestic demand, favourable government policies (PLI, Make in India), expanding manufacturing capability and the China+1 sourcing shift.
- Rising demand from end-use industries such as pharmaceuticals, FMCG, automotive, construction and electronics is expected to be a growth driver, tempered by volatility in crude oil and feedstock prices and stringent environmental/regulatory compliance requirements.
- Demand for the Company's pine-based chemical products is largely independent of crude oil prices, insulating it from petrochemical feedstock volatility that affects synthetic competitors.
- Camphor demand is supported by both traditional religious/spiritual use and growing application in pharmaceuticals, personal care, home care, wellness and industrial sectors, plus rising consumer preference for natural, sustainable, plant-based products.
